blocks.text: UniFlow is a modular single-page application built on **Quasar** and **Vue 3**, with **Firebase Authentication** and **Cloud Firestore** as a serverless backend. Route transitions pass through a boot-plugin guard that checks authentication and role, views dispatch to domain-specific **Pinia** stores, and the stores talk to Firebase through a service layer.

rows: 16 pages and 6 dialogs for faculties, departments, courses, users, and logs
Role-specific dashboards for Admin, Student, and Teacher
Collaborative group views, members, and shared resources
Real-time collaborative live share and chat panel
Classroom session creation, joining, and management
Task announcements, submissions, and grading rubrics
Personal todo lists and item trackers

items.text: Each protected route declares `meta.requiresAuth` and a `meta.roles` array in its module's `routes.js`.
The `boot/auth.js` plugin runs before each navigation and compares the route metadata with the current role in the Pinia user store.
Unauthenticated users are sent to `/auth/login`; users without the right role are sent to `/unauthorized`, before the view mounts.

blocks.text: Session creation runs a Firestore transaction in `firebaseService.js` that reads and increments a single `metadata/counters` document, so two sessions created at the same time never receive the same number. The cost is one extra read and write per session creation.

Each store is split into `index.js` (state and getters) and `action.js` (mutations and Firestore calls). Components never call the Firestore SDK directly, which keeps loading and error handling in one place per domain.
